summary: Recorded the client-completion result and promoted a durable Fact for the main finding. The re-propose comparison holds (evaluated index 11 of receipt f96da636a32f473280ce82dc0f0a002d): when the recovery replaced the live owner's command with the NOOP, handleCommit re-queued exactly the pending proposal (command id 77) on the owner's own propose channel and cleared its pending list, so the client's request is not silently consumed; the reply side is answered from source (replies come only from the execution path and only while the executing replica still holds proposals, epaxos/exec.go:126-138, which the owner just cleared), so the replaced instance produces no reply for that request and completion rests on the re-proposed request. No defect is claimed for that relationship, and its narrower cases (non-NONE replacement, failed owner, batching) are recorded as counterevidence and limits, together with the new source range for the reply condition and a partially explained gap about the reply side. The new Fact states the reusable conclusion of the recovery line of work: a replica lacking the instance's command can decide a value different from one a live replica has already committed, with its supporting behaviors referenced by exact revision. Remaining unfinished work: answering the newly registered gap explicitly and, if budget allows, measuring the re-proposed request's completion through the target's own execution path.
